identity: University of Amsterdam BA Griekse en Latijnse Taal en Cultuur, registry row 416 and RIO 56003, 2026–2027 ordinary regular-entry curriculum. The dated guide identifies Dutch and offers full-time and part-time enrolment. Dated course records establish English for some individual units.
sourceUse: The complete official table provides credits, components and choice status. The dated guide and first-year Greek and Latin, ACASA and thesis course records substantiate 2026–2027 identity, subject progression and specific conditions. The currently marketed joint degree begins in 2027–2028 according to VU, so its public-facing title and newer RIO do not supersede this cohort. The first-year compensating entry pathway is separate.

progression.first-year: Regular preparation, advancing from Greek and Latin acquisition into philosophical and rhetorical prose, tragedy and ancient philosophy. The public study plan reports a 48 EC binding advice threshold. The dated diagnostic writing assessment is mandatory and uncredited, and ACASA orientation is uncredited.
progression.second-year: Greek and Latin epic and linguistics, later literatures, the 6 EC ACASA excursion and the independent term paper.
progression.third-year: Three compulsory 6 EC courses, 30 EC elective or minor space, and a 12 EC thesis. The dated thesis record requires completion of all compulsory first- and second-year courses. The thesis colloquium is part of the thesis, with no separate credits.
